claims.why_not_priced: The author's own framing is 'I don't know if the market realized' - and the tape agrees with him: the stock is 1.57% above its 52-week low and 35.6% below its high three months after that post. A buyback that has retired 28% of the shares mechanically raises per-share cash and per-share earnings every quarter, and the quarterly release is where the run-rate and any new authorisation or dividend are disclosed. There is no news-search coverage of this ticker (n_queries=0 in every sweep), so no preview carries the net-cash arithmetic.

claims.finding: Briefing.com singled MOMO out on 2026-08-31 as one of only two names (with SWBI) whose option-implied volatility was 'signaling elevated expectations for near-term stock movement around this week's earnings... standing out against their historical volatility' - against a 20-day realised volatility of just 18.1%, the lowest of any name in this sample.
claims.why_not_priced: This one is priced, and that is the point of including it with zero signed impact: it is direct evidence that the option market is NOT complacent about this print, which caps how much any directional finding here can be worth and is why my number is small. It also tells me the realised-vol-based magnitude intuition (18.1% annualised implies roughly 1.1% a day) understates the event.
